physicalNotes: Radius 0.20251618 Jupiter radii from Castro-González et al. 2026 (2026arXiv260905413C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260905413C/abstract): 14,478.3 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0223391 Jupiter masses (Castro-González et al. 2026, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2026arXiv260905413C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260905413C/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Castro-González et al. 2026 (2026arXiv260905413C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname CASTRO_GONZALEZ_ET_AL_2026): P 1.4237828 d
sources.shape: Castro-González et al. 2026 (2026arXiv260905413C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname CASTRO_GONZALEZ_ET_AL_2026): a/R* 5.69; Castro-González et al. 2026 (2026arXiv260905413C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname CASTRO_GONZALEZ_ET_AL_2026): inclination 87.8 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Castro-González et al. 2026 (2026arXiv260905413C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname CASTRO_GONZALEZ_ET_AL_2026): transit mid-time 2459690.239 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 6 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
